pause_frame_sequence: 1. Receive MAC's RX FIFO crosses high-watermark; MAC Control sublayer constructs a PAUSE frame with DA = 01:80:C2:00:00:01, SA = own MAC, EtherType = 0x8808, opcode = 0x0001, pause_quanta = N (1 quantum = 512 BT).
2. PAUSE frame transmitted; partner receive MAC recognises and signals MAC Control.
3. Partner MAC Control stops the MAC's transmit FSM for N × 512 BT, allowing only previously-started frames to complete.
4. When the pause timer expires (or a PAUSE with quanta = 0 arrives), partner resumes transmission.
5. When the original receive FIFO drops below low-watermark, the receive-side MAC may send PAUSE with quanta = 0 to release.
collision_backoff_sequence_half_duplex: 1. COL asserts while TX_EN is asserted (collision during frame transmission).
2. MAC switches TXD to the 32-bit JAM pattern (any non-preamble pattern; spec recommends all-ones).
5. Compute backoff slots = uniform-random(0, 2^min(N,10)) — i.e. up to 2^N slots for N ≤ 10, capped at 1024 slots thereafter.
7. Return to TX_DEFER (wait for CRS = 0 + IFG) and retry the frame transmission.
8. If N reaches 16, abort and signal Excessive Collisions.
auto_negotiation_priority_resolution: After both sides have completed Base Page (+ optional Next Page) exchange, resolve highest common ability via the canonical priority order (decreasing): 1000BASE-T Full Duplex → 1000BASE-T Half Duplex → 100BASE-T2 Full Duplex → 100BASE-TX Full Duplex → 100BASE-T2 Half Duplex → 100BASE-T4 → 100BASE-TX Half Duplex → 10BASE-T Full Duplex → 10BASE-T Half Duplex.
PAUSE / Asym-PAUSE resolution per Annex 28B Table 28B-3: encode the combination of local + remote PAUSE bits into one of four states (TX_PAUSE on/off, RX_PAUSE on/off).
Once highest common ability is chosen, both ends configure their PMA / PMD accordingly and assert AutoNeg Complete (BMSR bit 1.5).

network_bring_up_sequence.description: ESC enters Init; reads SII into internal registers.
BRD to 0x0130 + 0x0010 returns total SubDevice count via WKC.
APRD to 0x0000 reads Type/Revision/Build per Position.
APWR to 0x0010 sets unique 16-bit FP address per SubDevice.
Optional: BWR 0x0900 latches RX timestamps; FPRD sweeps; compute delays.
FPWR 0x0810/0x0818, 0x0600+, DC SYNC0/1 cycle + start time.
Start cyclic LRD/LWR/LRW; Inputs valid; Outputs in Safe state.
FPWR 0x0120 = 0x08; arms PD WD; drives application outputs.
Cyclic LRD/LWR/LRW + ARMW (DC) + BRD 0x0130. On WKC drop → ERROR_HANDLING.

cyclic_frame_transmission_sequence.description: Construct frame: DA + SA + 0x88A4 + EtherCAT_Header + chained datagrams + FCS.
Decode datagram; if addressed, on-the-fly read/modify/write + WKC update; forward on Port 1.
Receive returning frame; verify WKC; extract Inputs.

mailbox_communication_sequence_coe_sdo_r.description: Construct CoE SDO Read Request: Mbx_Header + CoE Header + SDO Command.
FPWR 0x1000 (SM0 base); hardware sets Mbx_Out Empty=1.
Read SM0 via PDI; parse; look up Object Dictionary; construct response.
Write response into SM1; hardware sets Mbx_In Full=1.

distributed_clock_propagation_sequence.description: Per cycle: ARMW (Cmd 0x0D) with Position=0, Address=0x0910, Length=8.
ESC writes local System Time into Data field; WKC += 1.
Read Data field; update System Time Offset via PI loop.
SYNC0/SYNC1 align to local System Time; <100 ns jitter.

hot_connect_join_sequence.description: Auto-loopback opens; frame now passes through new device.
Next BRD sweep shows extra SubDevice.
APWR Configured Station Address; FPWR config; ESM walk to Op.
Hot Connect group's process data joins cyclic exchange.

cable_break_recovery_sequence_ring.description: MainDevice runs ring topology with two NICs. Both NICs send cyclic frames in opposite directions.
Cable break detected by ESC on affected port; auto-loopback closes the port.
Ring now splits into two healthy line segments; each MainDevice NIC reaches half the SubDevices via its primary direction.
Detects topology change via DL Status read; cyclic exchange continues without SubDevice loss.
